## Context
Latest official research confirms stable 4.x and current main route inventories are unchanged and fully mapped, but monica-cli exposes no industry-standard API document or deterministic edition compatibility report. Consumers must reverse-engineer internal reference JSON and cannot gate SDK generation on a validated contract.

## Delivery
- Enrich authoritative edition metadata from official routes, controllers, Scribe attributes, and resources.
- Export deterministic OpenAPI 3.1 for stable, next, or both editions with bearer security, parameters, request bodies, responses, unique operation IDs, CLI extensions, and source provenance.
- Add edition diff and contract validation commands with CI failure modes.
- Register output schemas and update help, docs, agent catalogs, read-only acceptance, and package/release tooling.

## Safety
Contract generation and validation are offline/read-only. Live acceptance remains GET-only with readOnlyMode enabled; credentials, identifiers, response bodies, and private topology stay outside Git, PM, logs, and GitHub.
Publish edition-aware OpenAPI and compatibility contracts

Generate validated OpenAPI 3.1 documents and deterministic stable-to-next compatibility diffs from authoritative Monica route references, with executable CLI links, source provenance, CI gates, agent-safe output, and current toolchain support.

OpenAPI 3.1 export covers all 172 stable endpoints and all 9 next endpoints with deterministic unique operation IDs, normalized path parameters, authentication, source provenance, CLI mapping, request/response metadata, and JSON/YAML interoperability; Edition diff reports added, removed, and changed operations deterministically and offers a failing CI gate for incompatible changes; Contract validation rejects duplicate operations, undeclared path parameters, invalid methods, missing mappings, stale provenance, and schema-invalid output without network or CRM writes; Default TOON plus JSON, YAML, Markdown, and table output remain schema-valid; help and docs describe exact commands and agent workflows; Exact 100/100/100/100 source coverage, 100 percent docstrings, under-300 code LOC, duplication/security/privacy/package/PM/release gates, and actual read-only monica acceptance all pass

All 62 PM items and verified histories reviewed; duplicate scan clear; official stable and main heads, routes, controllers, resources, and current package versions refreshed; clean branch based on v2026.7.26
Enable standard SDK generation, CI compatibility gates, and zero-guesswork agent integration across Monica API editions.
Consumers can adopt Monica APIs through a validated ecosystem-standard contract while detecting upstream edition drift before runtime.
Every authoritative Monica API operation is portable as OpenAPI and mechanically comparable across editions.
Endpoint parity is complete, so the highest-leverage remaining API enhancement is a portable validated contract instead of another bespoke wrapper.
Monica stable 4.x v4.1.2 and current main; monica-cli 2026.7.26; Bun 1.3.11; Node 22+; private instance read-only
Run monica api-research --help and monica schemas list: no OpenAPI export, edition diff, or cross-contract validation command exists despite complete bundled route references.
Agents, CI, and SDK generators can consume and validate a provenance-rich OpenAPI 3.1 document for either Monica edition and detect compatibility changes deterministically.
Only bespoke route references, coverage summaries, and source-status checks are available; external OpenAPI consumers and edition compatibility gates are absent.
Automated consumers must duplicate contract interpretation and cannot reliably detect breaking edition changes before deployment.
